correctness.rationale: Direct conditional propagation by commuting Pauli flips gives independent Bernoulli coordinates and exact Walsh moments. Stationary symmetric two-state telegraph forward equations give the explicit transform; all nonzero signed frequencies decay. Walsh inversion proves the complete limiting law and nonnegative zero-count criterion. Positive equal-frequency transform coefficients and an oscillatory mean-square lower bound establish the sharp logarithmic TV exponent in all damping regimes, with critical-root polynomial cases included. The optimized rate and three-body detuning coefficient follow from exact algebra. Independently constructed block density-matrix evolutions agree at 96 site values (maximum error 5.55e-16); finite tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A single perfectly correlated classical fluctuator does not force residual correlations: the complete long-time response is classified by exact signed-subset arithmetic. The (1,2,3) example has genuinely three-body parity memory while every one- and two-coordinate observable is uniform. The sharp optimal noise switching rate and detuning-inverse-square metastable regime are directly relevant to tuning and identifying correlated noise in synthetic quantum networks and are not just a renamed deterministic hypercube special case. The exact theorem has all-dimension real-weight scope, and its invariant is intrinsic to the measurable limiting site law.
